title: Support Surgeon: commandlet toolkit and playflow guardrails for safe admin operations
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Build a small, composable commandlet library ("Support Surgeon") and runtime shim to convert curated runbooks into first-class tasks with built-in safety rails. Goals: provide operators and SREs with compact, auditable admin primitives that can be invoked from the console, CI, or ad-hoc CLI while minimizing blast radius and preserving observability and audit trails. The scope covers: (1) a library of idempotent commandlets (drain-node, rotate-keys, flush-cache-prefix, rebuild-embedding-index, dataset-eviction), (2) a runbooks-as-tasks registry and manifest format, (3) RBAC + KMS-aware permission checks, (4) dry-run/simulate execution mode + approval gates, and (5) telemetry hooks for token-level cost attribution and operation tracing.
acceptance_criteria: 1) CLI/small binary that can run a registered runbook manifest with --dry-run and --simulate preserved side-effects; 2) every commandlet emits structured audit events to our admin-audit topic and appears in the Console's admin activity feed; 3) RBAC integration enforces that only users in the 'ops-admin' group can run destructive commandlets unless a two-step approval is recorded; 4) playflow guardrail prevents more than N concurrent drain/runbook executions per region; 5) documentation and runbook templates exist in Confluence; 6) integration tests and a canary pipeline for on-call invocation are implemented.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Kickoff: spike to evaluate implementation languages. Prototype drain-node as shell script and as Go commandlet. Outcome: Go binary preferred for single-distribution and static linking; Python wrapper for fast iteration of complex orchestration tasks.

2026-02-22 - Security sync (with SSO/KMS): agreed to require signed tokens for CLI invocations routed through the private control plane; ops-admin group mapping will be enforced via SCIM. Action: @Jordan to open infra ticket for SCIM mapping (in progress).

2026-02-28 - Safety trade-offs: discussed 'undo' semantics. Decided: every destructive commandlet must be reversible in two phases when possible; where not feasible, require a approval gate and create a snapshot (S3/Git) before proceeding.

2026-03-02 - Review feedback (PM): requested clearer UX for on-call flow. Implemented: --simulated-output flag and a structured summary JSON emitted pre-execution for the reviewer to inspect in the Console.

2026-03-05 - PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood/ops-tooling/pull/456 contains initial commandlet framework, manifest parser, and dry-run plumbing. Notes in PR: performance microbenchmarks for a drain-node loop; integration test skeleton added.
2026-03-07 - Telemetry update: added structured event schema for admin-audit. Need follow-up to wire token-level cost breakdown from runtime; filed ENG-880124 to track cost-attribution work.

2026-03-09 - Ops on-call trial: ran non-destructive cache flush via the CLI in dev region. Observed latency ~120ms median per commandlet call; logged to Grafana panel (link in dashboards). One flake: intermittent permission error due to stale SCIM mapping — mitigation: re-sync job scheduled daily (follow-up infra task).
2026-03-10 - Design review: reviewers approved guardrail thresholds but asked for automatic rollback strategies for multi-step runbooks; added to next sprint backlog as follow-up item.

Next steps: finish RBAC integration, complete two-step approval UX in Console, add canary pipeline that routes to a dedicated test pool, and expand commandlet catalog to include rotate-keys and index-rebuild.
